newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares close higher on foreign gains.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares close higher on foreign gains.

text.p: Swedish shares closed higher on Monday, buoyed by favourable international trends.
The firming U.S. dollar gave strength to the drug and forest sectors and a recovery in the debt market helped sentiment.
The Stockholm general index rose 2.42 percent to 2,674.83 in fairly light turnover worth 2.97 billion crowns.
The forestry sector climbed 3.67 percent on a stronger dollar and possible pulp price rise.
"In the middle of the month it could be on the agenda to announce price increases," Hans Burmeister, spokesman of Sodra unit Sodra Cell told Reuters.
MoDo jumps five crowns to 227, SCA climbs eight to 165.
The drugs sector was also a winner, rising 3.09 percent. Major player Astra gained 11 crowns to close at 358 crowns and Pharmacia & Upjohn jumped 12 crowns to 284 crowns.
Telecoms group Ericsson rose 7.5 to 254 crowns on expectations ahead of U.S. rival Motorola's report, due later on Monday, and after rising in the U.S. on Friday.
Car safety equipment company Autoliv rose sharply, up 14 to close at 314 crowns. This followed comments about
strong future growth from the head of Morton ASP, the Morton unit with which Autoliv is merging.
